newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU farm ministers to decide vet office status.
newsitem.headline: EU farm ministers to decide vet office status.

text.p: The status of the European Union's new veterinary office in Ireland is due to be decided by farm ministers meeting in Luxembourg next week.
"Ministers must choose beteen the Commission's proposal of creating a new agency or making it an extension of the Commission and therefore of the legislative process," an EU official said on Friday.
An advance team is already at Grange, near Dublin, preparing for the establishment of the new office.
Another question to be decided is how the office should be financed. The Commission has suggested that funding should come from a part of the fees for veterinary inspections.
"It will be up to ministers to decide whether this is the right way or whether there should be some other form of funding," the official said.

EU officials say that the office, which will carry out veterinary inspections at slaughterhouses and checks on plant and animal health, will help create equivalent veterinary standards throughout the European Union.
